Basic Visualizations

```{r}
# Load ggplot2 for better visualizations
library(ggplot2)

# Create a bar plot of workout types
ggplot(data, aes(x = Workout.Type)) +
  geom_bar() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Workout Types",
       x = "Workout Type",
       y = "Count")

# Create a histogram of calories burned
ggplot(data, aes(x = Calories.Burned)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 50, fill = "blue", alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Calories Burned",
       x = "Calories Burned",
       y = "Frequency")

# Create a boxplot of ca calories burned by workout type
ggplot(data, aes(x = Workout.Type, y = Calories.Burned)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Calories Burned by Workout Type",
       x = "Workout Type",
       y = "Calories Burned")

# Create a scatter plot
ggplot(data, aes(x = Workout.Duration..mins., y = Calories.Burned)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Workout Duration vs Calories Burned",
       x = "Duration (minutes)",
       y = "Calories Burned")


```


# Correlations Analysis

```{r correlations}
# Create a subset of numeric variables
numeric_data <- data[, c("Age", "Height..cm.", "Weight..kg.", 
                        "Workout.Duration..mins.", "Calories.Burned",
                        "Heart.Rate..bpm.", "Steps.Taken", "Distance..km.",
                        "Sleep.Hours", "Daily.Calories.Intake",
                        "Resting.Heart.Rate..bpm.")]

# Calculate correlations
correlations <- cor(numeric_data)

# View correlations (rounded to 2 decimal places)
round(correlations, 2)

# Create a basic correlation plot
library(corrplot)
corrplot(correlations, method = "color", 
         type = "upper", 
         addCoef.col = "black", # Add correlation coefficients
         number.cex = 0.7,      # Size of correlation coefficients
         tl.col = "black",      # Text label color
         tl.srt = 45)           # Rotate text labels

# Find strong correlations (absolute value > 0.5)
strong_correlations <- which(abs(correlations) > 0.5 & abs(correlations) < 1, arr.ind = TRUE)
print("Strong correlations (|r| > 0.5):")
for(i in 1:nrow(strong_correlations)) {
    row <- strong_correlations[i, 1]
    col <- strong_correlations[i, 2]
    if(row < col) {  # To avoid printing duplicates
        cat(sprintf("%s and %s: %.2f\n", 
                   colnames(numeric_data)[row],
                   colnames(numeric_data)[col],
                   correlations[row, col]))
    }
}

# Scatter plot for the strongest correlation
# Example for two variables (modify based on what you find):
ggplot(data, aes(x = Steps.Taken, y = Distance..km.)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    labs(title = "Steps Taken vs Distance",
         x = "Steps Taken",
         y = "Distance (km)")
```

## Distribution Analysis

```{r}

plot_distributions <- function(data) {
  for(col in names(data)) {
    p <- ggplot(data, aes_string(x = col)) +
      geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), bins = 30, fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
      geom_density(color = "red") +
      ggtitle(paste("Distribution of", col)) +
      theme_minimal()
    
    print(p)
  }
}

plot_distributions(numeric_cols)
```

###boxplots by gender


```{r}

create_gender_boxplots <- function(data) {
  # Select numeric columns (excluding User ID)
  numeric_cols <- names(data)[sapply(data, is.numeric)]
  numeric_cols <- numeric_cols[numeric_cols != "User.ID"]
  
  # Create boxplots for each numeric variable
  for(col in numeric_cols) {
    p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Gender, y = .data[[col]], fill = Gender)) +
      geom_boxplot() +
      theme_minimal() +
      labs(title = paste("Distribution of", gsub("\\.", " ", col), "by Gender"),
           y = col) +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
            plot.title = element_text(size = 12)) +
      scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2")
    
    print(p)
  }
}

# Create all boxplots
create_gender_boxplots(data)
```



### testing for mean differences


```{r}

data <- data %>%
  filter(Gender %in% c("Male", "Female"))

# Calculate BMI
data$BMI <- data$Weight..kg. / ((data$Height..cm. / 100)^2)

# Get summary statistics for height
height_summary <- data %>%
  group_by(Gender) %>%
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean_height = mean(Height..cm.),
    sd_height = sd(Height..cm.)
  )
print("Summary Statistics for Height:")
print(height_summary)

# Perform t-test for height
height_test <- t.test(Height..cm. ~ Gender, data = data)
print("\nT-test Results for Height:")
print(height_test)

# Perform t-test for weight
weight_test <- t.test(Weight..kg. ~ Gender, data = data)
print("\nT-test Results for Height:")
print(weight_test)

# Perform t-test for Workout.Duration..mins.
Duration_test <- t.test(Workout.Duration..mins. ~ Gender, data = data)
print("\nT-test Results for Height:")
print(Duration_test)

# Perform t-test for Calories.Burned
Calories.Burned_test <- t.test(Calories.Burned ~ Gender, data = data)
print("\nT-test Results for Height:")
print(Calories.Burned_test)

# Perform t-test for Heart.Rate..bpm.
Heart_test <- t.test(Heart.Rate..bpm. ~ Gender, data = data)
print("\nT-test Results for Height:")
print(Heart_test)

# Perform t-test for Steps.Taken
Steps.Taken_test <- t.test(Steps.Taken ~ Gender, data = data)
print("\nT-test Results for Height:")
print(Steps.Taken_test)


# Perform t-test for Distance..km.
Distance..km._test <- t.test(Distance..km. ~ Gender, data = data)
print("\nT-test Results for Height:")
print(Distance..km._test)

# Perform t-test for Sleep.Hours
Sleep.Hours_test <- t.test(Sleep.Hours ~ Gender, data = data)
print("\nT-test Results for Height:")
print(Sleep.Hours_test)

# Perform t-test for Daily.Calories.Intake
Daily.Calories.Intake_test <- t.test(Daily.Calories.Intake ~ Gender, data = data)
print("\nT-test Results for Height:")
print(Daily.Calories.Intake_test)

# Perform t-test for Resting.Heart.Rate..bpm.
Resting.Heart.Rate..bpm._test <- t.test(Resting.Heart.Rate..bpm. ~ Gender, data = data)
print("\nT-test Results for Height:")
print(Resting.Heart.Rate..bpm._test)

  geom_boxplot() +

       y = "Height (cm)") +
  theme_minimal()
```
